NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Prospect Capital Corporation (NASDAQ: PSEC) (“Prospect”), a leading business development company focused on investing in middle-market businesses, earlier this week completed the successful exit of its senior secured first lien term loan and preferred equity investment in Security Fire Systems (“SFS”), held by Safety Solutions Financing.

Prospect received cash exit proceeds of approximately $25 million for its investment in SFS. Prospect achieved a 41.8% realized gross annualized internal rate of return and a 1.2x multiple of invested capital through a combination of interest income, prepayment fees, equity distributions, and other cash flows.

SFS is an industry leader for fire security and protection, offering a comprehensive line of products and services, including automatic fire sprinkler design services, fire sprinkler system installation, system testing, system maintenance and servicing, remodel & retrofits, fire alarms and emergency response. SFS is certified to provide services in Texas, California, Arkansas, Colorado, and Oklahoma to multiple customer bases and end markets, consisting of hospitality, healthcare, education, retail, aviation, government, residential and religious properties.

“Our realization of this investment demonstrates our ability to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns by investing in the lower middle market,” said Angel Solis, Managing Director at Prospect.

About Prospect Capital Corporation

Prospect is a business development company that invests in middle market privately-held companies. Prospect’s investment objective is to generate both current income and long-term capital appreciation.

Prospect has elected to be treated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940. Prospect has elected to be treated as a regulated investment company under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

What You Should Know

  • A new collaboration between Bath & Body Works and Pantone blends trending colors with elevated fragrance in a limited-time collection for the holidays.   
  • Combining Bath & Body Works’ fragrance leadership with Pantone’s color authority, this modern assortment includes expertly crafted 3-wick candles and hand soaps in four distinct fragrances, designed for gifting or elevating any space in the home.
  • The trend-forward collection is available now for a limited time in Bath & Body Works stores and online.

COLUMBUS, Ohio, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bath & Body Works is collaborating with Pantone®, the global color authority, to launch a limited-edition fragrance collection designed for modern and trend-forward seasonal gifting and decorating.

The collection features four new seasonal fragrances, from cozy and comforting to fresh and woodsy, available in the brand’s expertly crafted 3-wick candles and hand soaps. Each scent is inspired by a signature color from a palette curated by Pantone, creating a distinctive and elevated look for the holiday season:

  • PANTONE 14-4307 Winter Sky: A cool and calming light blue is paired alongside crisp bergamot, frosted eucalyptus and cedarwood for a scent that feels like a breath of fresh wintry air.
  • PANTONE 12-0804 Cloud Cream: An elevated and soft white comes to life with notes of whipped milk, smooth vanilla and tonka for a warm and comforting fragrance that’s perfect for the holiday season.
  • PANTONE 19-1224 Fondue Fudge: This decadent gourmand featuring cocoa mousse and dark chocolate captures the depth and richness of this luxurious chocolate-brown hue.
  • PANTONE 19-4908 Magical Forest: Aromatic and fresh with a grounding warmth, rich amber, evergreen cedarwood and musk echo the mystery and depth of this dark, enchanting shade.

“This partnership brings together Pantone’s deep understanding about color in all forms and Bath & Body Works’ fragrance innovation for a fresh, modern collection to celebrate the season,” said Kristie Lewis, executive vice president of merchandising at Bath & Body Works. “With expertly crafted scents inspired by a trend-forward color palette, this elevated assortment is sophisticated yet inviting, perfect for gifting and decorating for the holidays.”

"Fragrance, like color, has the profound power to shift a mood, tell a story and transform an entire space," said Laurie Pressman, vice president of the Pantone Color Institute™. “In partnering with Bath & Body Works, we’ve woven the sensory magic of olfactory design with the visual language of color to curate a limited-edition collaboration for seasonal gifting and decorating, allowing trend conscious consumers to style their spaces with cohesive, beautiful layers of texture, color and scent."

Every Bath & Body Works scent is created with world-class perfumers, blending the art and science of fragrance. For gourmand scents that smell good enough to eat, like birthday cake, gooey brownies and chocolate fudge, the brand’s in-house experts also partner with leading fragrance houses and flavorists to capture their essence. That approach brought Fondue Fudge to life in a 3-wick candle and hand soap.

Bath & Body Works collaborated with Mane perfumer Jim Schmitt and flavorist Chris Williams to create Fondue Fudge for this collection.

“We set off to capture the irresistible indulgence of melted dark chocolate, beginning with Chris’s Dark Chocolate flavor,” said Schmitt. “I translated the rich cocoa and velvety smooth finish of his flavor inspiration into the Dark Chocolate Savor the Scent Accord™, evoking the deep, luscious brown of molten chocolate. Then we layered in facets of airy coco mousse, sweet amber and fluffy musk to reveal a sophisticated, irresistibly addictive fragrance that evokes the pleasure of dipping into warm chocolate fondue.”

For the collection’s other scents, Bath & Body Works collaborated with IFF on Cloud Cream and with dsm-firmenich on Winter Sky and Magical Forest.

The brand’s famous 3-wick candles are made from a premium soy wax blend infused with highly concentrated fragrance oils, offering up to 45 hours of room-filling scent. Bath & Body Works’ hand soaps are dermatologist approved* (*based on review of independent testing by board-certified dermatologist), made without sulfates, parabens and dyes, and made with Vitamin E, shea extract and aloe.

The collection is available online and in stores. For more information and to shop the Bath & Body Works and Pantone collection, visit bathandbodyworks.com.

PRODUCT DETAILS
The collection includes four new scents: Winter Sky, with crisp bergamot, frosted eucalyptus and cedarwood; Cloud Cream, with whipped milk, smooth vanilla and tonka; Fondue Fudge, with cocoa mousse and dark chocolate; and Magical Forest, with rich amber, evergreen cedarwood and musk. Each scent is available in hand soap ($8.95) and 3-wick candle ($24.95).

ABOUT BATH & BODY WORKS

Bath & Body Works is a global leader in personal care and home fragrance, driven by the belief that everybody deserves to feel good.

The brand’s beloved scents are expertly crafted for performance and a luxury fragrance experience. Formulated with thoughtfully chosen ingredients, Bath & Body Works body care products are available in multiple forms, including fine fragrance mist, body cream, lotion, eau de parfum, body wash, hand soap, sanitizer and more. The brand’s 3-wick candles are made with high-quality fragrance oils layered throughout a premium soy wax base for up to 45 hours of room-filling fragrance.

Consumers can shop Bath & Body Works in more than 1,900 stores in the U.S. and Canada, 550-plus international locations and select Ulta Beauty stores. Online, consumers can visit bathandbodyworks.com, Amazon and Ulta.com.

ABOUT PANTONE

Pantone provides the universal language of color that enables color-critical decisions through every stage of the workflow for brands and manufacturers. More than 10 million designers and producers around the world rely on Pantone products and services to help define, communicate and control color from inspiration to realization – leveraging advanced X-Rite technology to achieve color consistency across various materials and finishes for graphics, fashion and product design. Pantone Standards feature digital and physical color specification and workflow tools. The Pantone Color Institute™ provides customized color standards, brand identity and product color consulting as well as trend forecasting inclusive of Pantone Color of the Year, Fashion Runway Color Trend Reports, color psychology and more. Pantone B2B Licensing incorporates the Pantone Color System into different products and services, enabling licensees to communicate and reproduce certified Pantone values and improve efficiencies for their users. Pantone Lifestyle brings color and design together across apparel, home, and accessories. Learn more at www.pantone.com and connect with Pantone on Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn.

WATSONVILLE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Granite (NYSE: GVA) announced today the appointment of Stan Bass to its Board of Directors, effective November 17, 2026.

With more than 30 years of leadership experience in construction materials, operations, strategic growth, and business development, Mr. Bass brings significant industry expertise to support Granite's long-term strategy and continued expansion of its vertically integrated construction materials platform.

Throughout his career at Vulcan, Mr. Bass played a key role in the company's growth, leading organic and acquisition-driven expansion efforts that strengthened its position as the nation's largest producer of construction aggregates.

Sac-TMT is the first TROP2 ADC to improve OS compared to treatment of physician’s choice (TPC) in patients with advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who have received two or more prior lines of systemic therapy in a global Phase 3 study

TroFuse-015 is the second positive Phase 3 readout from the global TroFuse clinical development program evaluating sac-TMT across multiple tumor types

RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, today announced the pivotal Phase 3 TroFuse-015 trial evaluating sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), an investigational TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) licensed from Kelun-Biotech, met its primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) compared to treatment of physician’s choice (TPC, consisting of trifluridine-tipiracil, irinotecan, paclitaxel or docetaxel) in the treatment of patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who have received two or more prior lines of systemic therapy. TroFuse-015 represents the first time a TROP2-directed ADC has demonstrated an OS benefit in a global Phase 3 trial in this patient population, where there is significant unmet need. These data will be presented at an upcoming medical meeting and shared with regulatory authorities.

At final analysis, sac-TMT demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in OS compared to TPC for these patients who have received two or more prior lines of systemic therapy. Results were generally consistent across subgroups regardless of TROP2 expression status. Sac-TMT did not meet the secondary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Additionally, sac-TMT showed a nominally improved benefit in objective response rate (ORR), a secondary endpoint, favoring sac-TMT compared with TPC, but this was not formally tested under the prespecified analysis plan. The safety profile was consistent with what has been observed in previously reported studies of sac-TMT; no new safety signals were observed.

"Sac-TMT is the first TROP2 ADC to improve OS in a global Phase 3 study in advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma compared to TPC, demonstrating its potential in a particularly challenging disease setting,” said Dr. Marjorie Green, senior vice president and head of oncology, global clinical development, Merck Research Laboratories. "There is a tremendous unmet need for therapies that can improve survival for these patients. We look forward to discussing these data with regulatory authorities and sharing with the scientific community on behalf of patients who may benefit.”​

TroFuse-015 also marks the second positive Phase 3 study from Merck’s TroFuse clinical development program for sac-TMT. The program currently consists of 18 ongoing global Phase 3 trials across multiple tumor types, the broadest range of disease and treatment settings compared to any TROP2-directed ADC to date. The program is evaluating sac-TMT across a diverse range of tumor types, including endometrial, bladder, breast, cervical, gastric, non-small cell lung and ovarian cancers, and it spans early-to-late-stage disease as both monotherapy and in combination with immunotherapies. Within the program, 14 of the 18 Phase 3 studies are pursuing first-in-class opportunities to address unmet medical needs, including TroFuse-015.

About TroFuse-015
TroFuse-015 is a randomized, open-label, multicenter, global Phase 3 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06356311) evaluating the efficacy and safety of the TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) compared to the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in participants with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who have received two or more prior lines of systemic therapy. The trial enrolled 473 patients who were randomized to receive either sac-TMT or TPC, consisting of trifluridine-tipiracil, irinotecan, paclitaxel or docetaxel. Sac-TMT (4 mg/kg) was administered on Days 1, 15 and 29 of each six-week treatment cycle. Trifluridine-tipiracil (35 mg/m²) was administered orally twice daily on Days 1-5 and 8-12 of each four-week treatment cycle. Irinotecan (150 mg/m²) was administered on Days 1 and 15 of each four-week treatment cycle. Paclitaxel (80 mg/m²) was administered on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each four-week treatment cycle. Docetaxel (75 mg/m²) was administered on Day 1 of each three-week treatment cycle.

The study has a primary endpoint of overall survival. Secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, objective response rate, and duration of response.

About sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT)
Sac-TMT is an investigational TROP2-directed ADC with a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload and a unique bifunctional linker designed with the potential to maximize payload delivery to tumor cells and minimize payload loss while circulating in the body.

TROP2 is overexpressed on tumor cells compared to healthy cells in many common cancers, and through the TroFuse clinical development program, Merck is evaluating sac-TMT in 18 ongoing global Phase 3 trials across multiple tumor types, the broadest range of disease and treatment settings compared to any TROP2-directed ADC to date. The TroFuse development program spans early-to-late stage disease in more than nine disease areas and includes more than 15,000 patients worldwide. Numerous Phase 3 trials are exploring sac-TMT as monotherapy and in combination with immunotherapies, aiming to improve survival and quality of life for patients with advanced and earlier-stage cancers.

About Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma
Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma comprises gastric, gastroesophageal junction (GEJ), and esophageal adenocarcinomas (EAC).

Gastric (stomach) cancer often does not cause symptoms in its early stages, making it difficult to detect before the disease has advanced. Most gastric cancers are adenocarcinomas, accounting for approximately 90% to 95% of gastric malignancies, which develop from cells in the innermost lining of the stomach, known as the mucosa. In the U.S., it is estimated there will be approximately 31,500 new cases of gastric cancer and 10,700 deaths from the disease in 2026. Gastric cancer accounts for approximately 1.5% of all new cancers diagnosed in the U.S. each year.

Esophageal cancer starts when cells in the lining of the esophagus begin to grow out of control. In the U.S., about 68% of all new cases of esophageal cancer are EAC, and it is estimated there will be more than 14,300 new cases of EAC in 2026. Approximately 42% of EAC patients in the U.S. are diagnosed at the distant disease stage.

About the Merck and Kelun-Biotech Agreement
Sac-TMT was developed by Kelun-Biotech. Kelun-Biotech (6990.HK) is a holding subsidiary of Kelun Pharmaceutical (002422.SZ), which focuses on the R&D, manufacturing, commercialization and global collaboration of innovative biological drugs and small molecule drugs. Under an exclusive license and collaboration agreement, Kelun-Biotech has granted Merck the exclusive rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize sac-TMT in all territories outside of Greater China (which includes Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan).

Merck’s focus on cancer
Every day, we follow the science as we work to discover innovations that can help patients, no matter what stage of cancer they have. As a leading oncology company, we are pursuing research where scientific opportunity and medical need converge, underpinned by our diverse pipeline of more than 20 novel mechanisms. With one of the largest clinical development programs across more than 25 tumor types, we strive to advance breakthrough science that will shape the future of oncology. By addressing barriers to clinical trial participation, screening and treatment, we work with urgency to reduce disparities and help ensure patients have access to high-quality cancer care. Our unwavering commitment is what will bring us closer to our goal of bringing life to more patients with cancer. For more information, visit https://www.merck.com/research/oncology.

About Merck
At Merck, known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, we are unified around our purpose: We use the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world. For more than 130 years, we have brought hope to humanity through the development of important medicines and vaccines. We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company in the world – and today, we are at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. We foster a diverse and inclusive global workforce and operate responsibly every day to enable a safe, sustainable and healthy future for all people and communities. Key Terms

antibody-drug conjugatemedical
An antibody-drug conjugate is a targeted medicine that combines an antibody, which can identify specific cells, with a powerful drug designed to destroy those cells. This approach allows for precise treatment, minimizing damage to healthy tissue. For investors, developments in this area can signal advances in cancer therapies and potential growth opportunities in the biotech sector.
overall survivalmedical
Overall survival is the average or median length of time patients remain alive after starting a treatment or entering a clinical study, measured regardless of cause of death. Investors care because it is a clear, hard measure of a therapy’s real-world benefit — like timing how long a new battery actually runs — and strong improvements in overall survival can drive regulatory approval, market adoption and revenue potential.
progression-free survivalmedical
Progression-free survival is the length of time during and after a treatment that a patient's disease does not get worse, measured from the start of treatment until the disease shows measurable signs of progression or the patient dies. Investors care because longer progression-free survival in clinical trials often signals that a drug is effective, improving chances of regulatory approval, market adoption, and revenue potential—think of it as a stopwatch showing how long a therapy can keep the illness at bay.
blinded independent central reviewmedical
Blinded independent central review is a quality-control step in clinical trials where outside medical experts, who do not know which patients received the experimental therapy, re-examine key measurements (like scans or lab results) to prevent bias. Think of it as neutral referees watching game footage without knowing the teams, which gives investors greater confidence that the trial results are fair, more reliable for regulators, and less likely to be overturned or disputed.
open-labelmedical
Open-label describes a situation where everyone involved in a study or process knows the full details, such as who is receiving a treatment or intervention. For investors, understanding whether a project or product is open-label helps gauge the level of transparency and potential biases, influencing trust and decision-making. It’s like knowing whether a test or experiment is conducted openly or behind closed doors.

Additional Highlights:

  • Total comparable club sales increased by 13.5% and 10.6% in the third quarter and first nine months of fiscal 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in fiscal 2025. Excluding the impact of gasoline sales, comparable club sales increased by 4.1% and 2.9% in the third quarter and first nine months of fiscal 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in fiscal 2025.
  • Membership fee income increased to $138.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $126.3 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Membership fee income increased to $406.3 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $370.0 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2025. The increase in both comparative periods was primarily driven by strength in membership acquisition, retention and higher-tier membership penetration across both new and existing clubs.
  • Gross profit increased to $1.02 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $1.01 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Merchandise gross margin rate, which excludes gasoline sales and membership fee income, decreased by approximately 170 basis points compared to the third quarter of fiscal 2025 primarily driven by promotional activities, principally associated with the Company’s 42nd birthday celebration event. Gross profit increased to $3.16 billion in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $2.99 billion in the first nine months of fiscal 2025. Merchandise gross margin rate decreased by approximately 70 basis points compared to the first nine months of fiscal 2025 primarily driven by promotional activities associated with the Company’s 42nd birthday celebration event, partially offset by tariff refund benefits recognized in the first half of fiscal 2026.
  • Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) decreased to $696.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $788.2 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. SG&A increased to $2.35 billion in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $2.34 billion in the first nine months of fiscal 2025. SG&A in both periods included a benefit of approximately $240 million, net of associated legal fees, recognized in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, from a settlement to resolve litigation related to credit card interchange fees in which the Company was the plaintiff. The Company recognized an estimated $95 million of expenses related to the use of proceeds from the settlement, which partially offset the benefit. Gains from sale-leaseback transactions in the second and third quarters of fiscal 2026 also favorably impacted SG&A. Partially offsetting these favorable items were increases in labor, occupancy, and operational costs primarily as a result of new club and gas station openings.
  • Income tax expense increased to $83.0 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $56.0 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Income tax expense increased to $201.2 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $154.2 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2025.
  • Net income increased to $219.5 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $152.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Net income increased to $536.1 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $452.5 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2025.
  • Adjusted EBITDA increased by 39.9% to $421.6 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $301.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Adjusted EBITDA increased by 19.7% to $1.07 billion in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 compared to $891.1 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2025.
  • Under its existing share repurchase program, the Company repurchased 376,942 shares of common stock, totaling $35.6 million, inclusive of associated costs, in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026, the Company repurchased 3,875,220 shares of common stock, totaling $366.3 million, inclusive of associated costs. Approximately $386.9 million remained available to purchase under such program.

Fiscal 2026 Ending January 30, 2027 Outlook

“Our third quarter reflects strong execution across the business, with comparable sales accelerating,” said Laura Felice, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer, BJ’s Wholesale Club. “We invested meaningfully for our stakeholders while continuing to grow the business, and we are raising our full-year guidance for both comparable sales and adjusted EPS. With a strong balance sheet, we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable, profitable growth.”

Note Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Information

This press release includes financial measures that are not calculated in accordance with GAAP, including adjusted net income, adjusted net income per diluted share (“adjusted EPS”), adjusted EBITDA, adjusted free cash flow, net debt, net debt to last twelve months (“LTM”) adjusted EBITDA, and other key performance indicators, including comparable club sales, which includes all clubs that were open for at least 13 months at the beginning of the period and were in operation during the entirety of both periods being compared, including relocated clubs and expansions.

We define adjusted net income as net income as reported, adjusted for non-recurring, infrequent, or unusual charges, including restructuring charges, and other adjustments that the Company believes appropriate, net of the tax impact of such adjustments.

We define adjusted EPS as adjusted net income divided by the weighted-average diluted shares outstanding.

We define adjusted EBITDA as net income before interest expense, net, provision for income taxes, and depreciation and amortization, adjusted for the impact of certain other items, including stock-based compensation expense, restructuring, and other adjustments.

We define adjusted free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities less additions to property and equipment, net of disposals, plus proceeds from sale-leaseback transactions.

We define net debt as total debt outstanding less cash and cash equivalents.

We define net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA as net debt at the balance sheet date divided by adjusted EBITDA for the trailing twelve-month period.

We present adjusted net income, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA, which are not recognized financial measures under GAAP, because we believe such measures assist investors and analysts in comparing our operating performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance.

We believe that adjusted net income, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA are helpful in highlighting trends in our core operating performance compared to other measures, which can differ significantly depending on long-term strategic decisions regarding capital structure, the tax jurisdictions in which companies operate, and capital investments. We use adjusted net income, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA to supplement GAAP measures of performance in the evaluation of the effectiveness of our business strategies; to make budgeting decisions; and to compare our performance against that of other peer companies using similar measures. We also use adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS in connection with establishing annual and long-term incentive compensation.

We present adjusted free cash flow, which is not a recognized financial measure under GAAP, because we use it to report to our Board of Directors and we believe it assists investors and analysts in evaluating our liquidity. We present net debt and net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA, which are not recognized as financial measures under GAAP, because we use them to report to our Board of Directors and we believe they assist investors and analysts in evaluating our borrowing capacity. Net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA is a key financial measure that is used by management to assess the borrowing capacity of the Company.

Platform designed to address growing demand for critical-mineral pricing intelligence, geopolitical supply-risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and procurement transparency

Initial focus on tungsten and antimony, with potential expansion into rare earths, semiconductors and other defense-critical materials

VisionWave intends to pursue near-term revenue opportunities through subscription-based intelligence services, compliance documentation and transaction-related services

WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VisionWave Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: VWAV) (“VisionWave” or the “Company”), a technology company developing advanced defense, autonomous systems and artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the acquisition of the Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform (“CMIP”), a specialized technology platform designed to provide market intelligence, supply-chain transparency, regulatory screening and procurement-related information for strategically important critical minerals.

The agreement with Litial Ltd was signed on November 18, 2026, and the acquisition has not yet closed. If completed, the acquisition would mark VisionWave's entry into the defense-industrial supply-chain intelligence market and is intended to establish a new commercial technology offering with the potential to generate recurring revenue through subscriptions, compliance-related services and transaction-based fees.

Unlike technologies requiring extensive hardware development or manufacturing infrastructure before commercialization, CMIP's software- and data-driven architecture is designed to support deployment through digital services and enterprise workflows.

According to the technology developer's materials, CMIP includes a browser-based minimum viable product (MVP) supporting benchmark monitoring, counterparty screening and compliance-document generation. VisionWave intends, following the closing of the acquisition, to evaluate these capabilities for commercial deployment and pursue initial revenue opportunities following technical, cybersecurity and regulatory validation.

The platform initially focuses on tungsten and antimony, two materials of strategic importance to defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing. VisionWave also sees potential to extend the platform to other critical minerals, specialized industrial materials and defense-related components.

Addressing a Strategic Challenge in Defense and Industrial Supply Chains

Critical minerals have become increasingly important to national security, defense readiness, industrial resilience and international trade.

Tungsten is used in applications including aerospace components, wear-resistant materials, cutting equipment and ammunition. Antimony is used in specialized industrial and defense-related applications.

Both minerals appear on the United States' 2025 Critical Minerals List and the European Union's critical raw materials list, reflecting their economic importance and exposure to supply-chain vulnerabilities.

Global supply chains for these materials face several structural challenges:

  • Geopolitical supply concentration: Significant production and processing capacity is concentrated in a limited number of countries, creating potential exposure to geopolitical developments and trade restrictions.
  • Export controls and sanctions: International restrictions can affect material availability, supplier eligibility and cross-border transactions.
  • Pricing complexity: Market participants must navigate different material grades, delivery conditions, geographic markets and pricing methodologies.
  • Limited supply-chain visibility: Identifying the origin, processing history and chain of custody of strategically important materials can be challenging.
  • Fragmented procurement information: Pricing, counterparty verification, regulatory screening and material provenance are often handled through separate systems.

China's export restrictions on antimony-related products in 2024 and selected tungsten-related products in 2025 have further highlighted the strategic importance of supply-chain intelligence.

VisionWave believes these developments create an opportunity for technology platforms capable of combining market data, regulatory information, supplier intelligence and transaction documentation to support more informed procurement and risk-management decisions.

CMIP: An Integrated Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform

CMIP is designed as a specialized market-intelligence and workflow platform rather than simply a commodity trading application.

Its architecture brings together four complementary capabilities intended to help organizations understand critical-mineral markets, evaluate counterparties, document transactions and monitor supply-chain exposure.

1. Critical Minerals Pricing and Market Intelligence

CMIP includes a proposed benchmark pricing framework covering tungsten ammonium paratungstate (APT), antimony trioxide and antimony metal.

The framework is designed to support structured price monitoring, documented pricing methodologies and market comparisons.

By combining market pricing information with other supply-chain and transaction data, CMIP aims to support procurement planning, commercial negotiations and material sourcing decisions.

2. Regulatory Compliance and Sanctions Intelligence

The platform incorporates automated counterparty-screening workflows designed to reference relevant sanctions and restricted-party information, including U.S., European Union and United Nations sources.

Its compliance infrastructure is intended to support counterparty identity and sanctions screening, export-control information workflows, documentation of screening results and regulatory risk indicators, and compliance-related records and audit trails.

These capabilities are intended to assist compliance professionals and procurement organizations, rather than replace required legal determinations or regulatory approvals.

3. Controlled Counterparty and Transaction Network

CMIP includes a proposed closed over-the-counter network designed to connect prequalified commercial participants in strategically important materials markets.

The network architecture contemplates business-identity verification, sanctions screening, controlled participant access and structured transaction workflows.

VisionWave believes this approach could help support more transparent and accountable interactions among mineral producers, processors, traders, industrial buyers and defense-related procurement organizations.

4. Material Provenance and Supply-Chain Traceability

A central element of CMIP's long-term strategy is the development of structured data linking materials to their origins, processing history, counterparties and transaction records.

This information could enable organizations to evaluate where a critical material originated, which suppliers and intermediaries handled it, whether counterparties are subject to restrictions, and how geopolitical developments affect sourcing risks.

VisionWave believes the ability to connect material provenance, regulatory information and procurement intelligence could become an important differentiating capability as the platform develops and accumulates appropriately licensed transaction data.

Near-Term Revenue Opportunities and Commercialization Strategy

VisionWave intends to prioritize the commercialization of CMIP through three complementary revenue channels:

  • Annual subscriptions: Recurring fees for access to critical-minerals pricing intelligence, supplier-risk information, compliance tools and related services.
  • Transaction-related fees: Potential revenue from facilitating transactions through the platform's controlled counterparty network.
  • Compliance documentation services: Fees associated with screening records, documentation workflows and transaction-related compliance support.

The platform developer's proposed commercial model contemplates annual enterprise subscriptions ranging from approximately $25,000 to $75,000, transaction fees of approximately 0.25%–0.5% of matched transactions, and compliance-documentation fees of approximately $500–$2,000 per service.

These figures represent proposed pricing assumptions rather than established customer contracts or verified historical revenue. VisionWave has not independently validated these assumptions, and there can be no assurance that any customer will purchase services at these or any other prices.

VisionWave intends to pursue early commercial opportunities using the platform's existing software capabilities while evaluating additional functionality, regulatory requirements and customer needs.

The Company's objective is to establish an initial revenue-generating business and subsequently expand the platform's customer base, data coverage and integration with VisionWave's broader intelligence technologies.

Commercial deployment and the timing of any revenue generation remain subject to technical validation, customer adoption and applicable regulatory requirements.

Potential Integration with StratumAI: Toward Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence

VisionWave intends to evaluate connecting CMIP with its StratumAI intelligence architecture to develop more advanced defense supply-chain intelligence capabilities.

The proposed integration would seek to combine critical-minerals data, regulatory information, geopolitical developments and AI-supported analysis to create a more comprehensive defense-industrial intelligence capability.

Potential applications include supplier-risk monitoring, commodity price and availability intelligence, sanctioned-party detection, geopolitical supply-risk analysis, provenance review, alternative-source identification and procurement alerts.

The Company believes this approach could extend the application of AI-driven intelligence beyond physical sensing and autonomous systems into the materials and industrial supply chains that support defense technologies.

Over time, VisionWave may evaluate expanding the platform beyond tungsten and antimony to other strategically important materials and components, including rare earth elements, gallium, germanium, graphite, titanium, specialized alloys, semiconductors, electronic components and defense manufacturing inputs.

Such expansion would be subject to additional technology development, data availability, regulatory requirements and commercial validation.

Acquisition Terms and Strategic Commercial Support

Under the acquisition agreement, VisionWave has agreed to acquire CMIP from Litial Ltd for $11 million in deferred consideration, to be evidenced by an unsecured, subordinated, non-interest-bearing promissory note to be delivered at closing.

The purchase consideration is payable in two installments of $5.5 million on the first and second anniversaries of closing, subject to defined revenue milestones.

Both installments are contingent upon CMIP generating qualifying revenue of at least $500,000 during the first three months following closing and an additional $1 million during the subsequent three months. If either milestone is not achieved, both installments are forfeited. The closing of the acquisition is subject to customary conditions and to VisionWave's receipt of an independent third-party valuation of CMIP supporting the purchase price, which has not yet been delivered and which may not be waived by either party. Either party may terminate the agreement if the closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026. There can be no assurance that the valuation will support the purchase price or that the acquisition will be completed.

The acquisition is structured without an upfront cash payment or issuance of VisionWave common shares.

VisionWave also entered into a two-year strategic engagement agreement with DNE International FZ LLC to provide advisory and administrative support relating to CMIP's commercial development and operational planning.

DNE's $3.8 million contractual compensation is evidenced by a subordinated, unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note and is subject to the same CMIP revenue milestones and other contractual conditions, and will be cancelled if the CMIP acquisition does not close by March 31, 2027.

The Company believes the transaction structure preserves equity capital while aligning the acquisition consideration and related advisory compensation with defined commercial performance. Additional information regarding these agreements is included in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Additional Acquisition of AI-Powered Video Intelligence Technology

Separately, on November 18, 2026, VisionWave completed the $4 million acquisition of MoreSpeed, an AI-powered forensic video search technology, from SofTech Resources Limited.

MoreSpeed is designed to accelerate the identification of relevant persons, vehicles and events within large video repositories through an AI-based search and prioritization architecture.

Developer-supplied benchmarks reported median search acceleration of approximately 18.8 times against the tested baseline, which VisionWave has not independently verified and which remain subject to the Company's post-closing verification of the delivered assets.

VisionWave intends to evaluate MoreSpeed for potential integration with its existing xCalibre video analytics and broader intelligence technology portfolio.

The acquisition consideration is payable through an unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note due on the first anniversary of closing, subject to contractual protections. Unlike the CMIP consideration, the MoreSpeed payment obligation is not contingent on future revenue.

Management Commentary

Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave Holdings, commented:

“Critical minerals are becoming an increasingly important component of national security, defense readiness and industrial resilience. The challenge is no longer simply obtaining these materials, but understanding where they originate, who controls their supply, how geopolitical developments affect availability, and whether procurement decisions can be supported by reliable and transparent information.

“With the planned acquisition of CMIP, we expect to enter a strategically important intelligence market that complements our broader defense technology vision.

“We believe the opportunity extends beyond conventional commodity pricing. Our objective is to bring together market intelligence, regulatory screening, supply-chain provenance and AI-supported analysis into an integrated environment that can help organizations better understand critical-material sourcing risks.

“Importantly, our near-term priority is commercialization. The platform's existing software capabilities and proposed subscription, transaction and compliance-service revenue models provide a foundation for pursuing early commercial opportunities without requiring the extensive manufacturing infrastructure associated with hardware-based products.

“CMIP also creates a potential new intelligence domain for StratumAI, allowing us to explore applications in defense procurement, supplier-risk analysis, geopolitical monitoring and strategic materials intelligence.

“We see the initial focus on tungsten and antimony as a starting point, with the longer-term potential to address a broader range of critical minerals, electronic components and industrial supply-chain dependencies.

“We have structured the acquisition without upfront cash consideration or equity issuance, with the purchase price tied to defined commercial revenue milestones.

“Our strategy is to acquire and develop differentiated intellectual property that can address meaningful operational challenges, generate commercial opportunities and create long-term value for VisionWave and its shareholders.”

About VisionWave Holdings, Inc.

VisionWave Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: VWAV) is a technology company developing dual-use unmanned systems, autonomous capabilities, and advanced sensing solutions for defense, security, and commercial applications. Its portfolio includes the VARAN unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) platform and a suite of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and drone solutions, supported by sensing, perception, and autonomy technologies. Through technology development and strategic partnerships, VisionWave aims to deliver integrated ground and aerial systems that enhance situational awareness, support operational missions, and reduce personnel exposure to risk across military and civilian environments. For more information, visit https://www.vwav.inc.

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, including statements concerning the anticipated closing of the CMIP acquisition, the receipt and conclusions of the independent valuation of CMIP, the anticipated benefits of the CMIP and MoreSpeed acquisitions, potential integration with StratumAI and xCalibre, the DNE engagement, near-term commercialization plans, the development of critical-minerals intelligence technologies, future customer adoption, revenue opportunities, expansion into additional materials markets and VisionWave's strategic objectives.

Forward-looking statements are based on current expectations, assumptions and estimates and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied.

These risks include, among others, the risk that the independent valuation of CMIP is not delivered or does not support the purchase price and that the CMIP acquisition is not completed, the risk that the MoreSpeed assets are not delivered or do not perform as represented, challenges relating to technology integration, intellectual property and data ownership, third-party software and data licensing, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, the validity and acceptance of proposed compliance workflows, competition from established market-data providers, the ability to establish active counterparty networks, customer adoption, the achievement of CMIP revenue milestones, the commercialization of acquired technologies, financing and liquidity constraints, including the Company's ability to pay the promissory notes when due, and other risks described in the Company's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

FISHERS, IN / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC) ("American Resources") and ReElement Technologies Corporation ("ReElement"), a leading U.S. operator of advanced critical mineral refining and separation technologies in which American Resources maintains a strategic minority ownership interest, today announced that the Frontier Minerals Consortium ("Frontier"), of which both companies are members, has been selected by the Government of Kenya as the successful bidder in the competitive international tender for the Mrima Hill Niobium, Rare Earth Elements and Other Minerals Development Project in Kwale County, Kenya.

The selection, announced by Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs, represents a significant milestone in advancing one of the world's most strategically important undeveloped rare earth and niobium deposits. Frontier has been selected to enter exclusive negotiations toward a prospecting license, with subsequent activities subject to applicable regulatory approvals, community engagement and licensing requirements.

Frontier is partnered with American Resources, ReElement and Bunker Hill Silver Corp. ("Bunker Hill"), bringing together complementary expertise in mineral resource development, critical minerals supply chains and advanced refining technologies. The consortium's integrated approach is designed to support the development of a comprehensive mine-to-material value chain, emphasizing domestic processing and refining, local economic participation and long-term value creation in Kenya.

Through its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources serves as a strategic supply-chain and commercial development partner, connecting mineral resource opportunities with advanced processing and refining capabilities, including those of ReElement, and downstream markets.

As part of its participation in the consortium, American Resources expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements among the consortium partners. ReElement participates as the consortium's advanced refining technology partner, contributing its proprietary chromatography-based separation and purification capabilities, with the opportunity to generate refining-related revenues through future technology deployment, processing and commercial arrangements, subject to feasibility studies and definitive agreements.

The consortium is pursuing a capital-efficient development strategy that includes potential non-dilutive financing, government-supported funding and other strategic financing alternatives. Consistent with its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier while minimizing direct capital requirements and actively supporting the consortium through feasibility and development. This approach is designed to create long-term economic value for American Resources and its shareholders while advancing Kenya's critical mineral development and in-country value-chain objectives, subject to definitive agreements.

A Differentiated Mine-to-Material Development Strategy

A central component of Frontier's proposal is the development of an integrated critical minerals value chain within Kenya, extending beyond traditional resource extraction and concentrate exports to include domestic mineral processing, advanced separation and refining, workforce development and downstream market integration.

The consortium's selection reflects a proposal designed to address Kenya's stated objectives for domestic mineral beneficiation, local economic participation, environmental stewardship and responsible resource development.

American Resources contributes its international resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, strategic partnerships and critical minerals supply-chain development capabilities. ReElement contributes its proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and refining platform, designed to produce high-purity, specification-grade rare earth elements and other critical minerals through modular, scalable processing systems. Bunker Hill contributes mining, engineering, metallurgical processing and project development expertise, providing an integrated approach to evaluating and potentially developing the Mrima Hill resource.

Together, these capabilities are intended to support the development of a commercially sustainable supply chain that retains more economic value in Kenya while expanding access to strategically important critical minerals for U.S. and allied manufacturers.

Advanced U.S. Refining Technology Supporting Kenyan Value Creation

ReElement's chromatography-based technology represents a differentiated approach to critical mineral refining, utilizing water-based separation processes designed to reduce chemical consumption, energy requirements and environmental impacts compared with conventional solvent extraction methods.

Originally developed at Purdue University and licensed in 2021, the technology has since been advanced and commercialized through ReElement's proprietary research, engineering and intellectual property development. ReElement has validated separation and purification capabilities across 15 rare earth elements and additional critical minerals, achieving purities of up to 99.999% for select products.

The company commissioned its first commercial-scale chromatography columns for germanium production at the facility in August 2026 and continues to progressively scale its domestic refining capabilities.

ReElement's proposed role in the Mrima Hill project will focus on developing optimized commercial processing and refining flowsheets utilizing its proprietary chromatography-based technology. This approach is designed to support the phased deployment of modular refining infrastructure in Kenya, enabling the production of high-purity, value-added critical mineral products within the country, subject to project-specific technical, commercial and regulatory requirements. Beyond Mrima Hill, ReElement's participation is expected to create opportunities to evaluate additional critical mineral feedstocks throughout Kenya and the broader region, with the objective of leveraging potential shared refining infrastructure, enhancing capital efficiency and technology utilization, and supporting Kenya's emergence as a regional hub for advanced critical mineral refining.

This approach is intended to support the production of higher-value refined materials within Kenya rather than limiting the country's participation to the export of raw minerals or intermediate concentrates.

A Strategic Opportunity for Kenya and the United States

Mrima Hill contains historically identified rare earth and niobium mineralization, including elements important to permanent magnets, aerospace, advanced electronics and other strategic industries. Historical mineral resource estimates indicate significant mineralization; however, these estimates have not been verified as current mineral resources and will require further technical evaluation.

The project represents an opportunity to align Kenya's economic development and industrialization objectives with the United States' strategic interest in building diversified, secure, transparent and traceable critical mineral supply chains.

By supporting domestic processing and refining, the consortium's proposed development model seeks to create opportunities for Kenyan workers, technical professionals, suppliers and local communities while establishing additional sources of high-value critical materials for international manufacturers.

Mark C. Jensen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Resources Corporation, commented: "This selection represents much more than an important milestone for the Frontier Minerals Consortium. It reflects a shared vision of how critical mineral resources can be developed to create lasting economic value for resource-rich countries while strengthening the industrial and national security interests of the United States and its allies.

"For too long, many resource-rich nations have participated primarily at the extraction stage of the global minerals supply chain, while much of the downstream processing, refining and economic value has been captured elsewhere. We believe the opportunity at Mrima Hill is to help change that model by bringing together world-class mining capabilities, advanced American refining technology and integrated supply-chain development.

"Our Platform Orchestration model is designed to create meaningful economic participation in strategic resource opportunities through partnerships and equity interests, while leveraging third-party capital and minimizing direct development expenditures. We believe this approach allows American Resources to participate in globally significant projects while remaining focused on capital efficiency and the creation of long-term shareholder value.

"Importantly, this announcement is not the culmination of our efforts, but the beginning of a much broader opportunity. We look forward to working alongside the Government of Kenya, local communities and our consortium partners to advance a responsible, commercially sustainable development strategy that creates meaningful value for Kenya and strengthens critical mineral supply chains for the United States. We believe this collaborative approach can serve as a model for mutually beneficial partnerships in other resource-rich jurisdictions where we are actively developing relationships and opportunities."

Next Steps

Following the Government of Kenya's selection, Frontier intends to advance the required community engagement, regulatory and prospecting-license application processes in accordance with Kenyan law.

Subject to receipt of the necessary approvals, the consortium's proposed development program includes confirmation drilling, updated mineral resource evaluation, metallurgical test work, refining technology assessments, environmental and social studies, and preparation of a bankable feasibility study.

The feasibility process will focus on developing integrated mining, mineral processing and advanced refining flowsheets, leveraging ReElement's proprietary chromatography-based platform to support the production of high-purity, value-added critical minerals within Kenya. This approach is designed to establish a commercially viable, mine-to-material development model that maximizes in-country value-chain capture while supporting diversified critical mineral supply chains for the United States and its allies.

The consortium recognizes the environmental, cultural and social significance of Mrima Hill and intends to work with Kenyan authorities, local communities and other stakeholders to evaluate the project responsibly and in accordance with applicable requirements.

About American Resources Corporation

American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC) operates a diversified critical materials platform through its Platform Orchestration strategy, which coordinates complementary capabilities across commercial feedstock origination, resource sourcing, industrial processing and advanced refining partnerships. This capital-efficient approach enables the Company to align resources, technologies and commercial relationships to evolving customer requirements and national priorities while strengthening U.S. and allied critical mineral supply chains.

The Company's operating platforms span conventional and unconventional resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, recycling, processing and conditioning, complemented by its strategic ownership interest in ReElement Technologies Corporation, a leading U.S. advanced materials transformation and refining company. Through these complementary capabilities and strategic relationships, American Resources seeks to connect diverse feedstock sources with advanced processing and refining solutions, enabling greater value chain capture and supporting growing commercial, industrial and defense-sector demand.

American Resources' modular, asset-light business model emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, scalable operations and strategic partnerships. By coordinating specialized capabilities across the critical materials value chain without requiring traditional vertical integration, the Company seeks to expand commercial opportunities and support resilient, economically sustainable supply chains serving infrastructure, defense, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, energy and electrification markets.

For more information, visit americanresourcescorp.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

About ReElement Technologies Corporation

ReElement Technologies Corporation, a strategic portfolio holding of American Resources Corporation (NASDAQ:AREC), is a leading U.S. developer and operator of advanced materials transformation and refining technologies. Its modular, refining-first platform utilizes proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and purification technology to transform diverse feedstocks - including primary mineral concentrates, recycled materials, industrial byproducts and other unconventional sources - into high-purity, specification-grade critical materials. ReElement's flexible technology enables the co-location of advanced refining capabilities closer to feedstock sources and downstream customers, supporting greater value chain capture while reducing chemical consumption and environmental impact. The Company supports secure, resilient U.S. and allied supply chains serving defense, aerospace, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, permanent magnets, energy and battery technologies.

For more information, visit reelementtech.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable securities laws, including statements regarding the Frontier Minerals Consortium's selection, the proposed Mrima Hill project, licensing and regulatory approvals, community engagement, mineral resource evaluation, feasibility studies, financing, future mining and refining activities, potential deployment of ReElement's technology, anticipated equity participation and commercial arrangements, anticipated economic benefits and the development of critical mineral supply chains.

SINGAPORE, SG / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Ryde Group Ltd (NYSE American:RYDE) ("Ryde" or the "Company"), a leading technology platform for mobility and quick commerce headquartered in Singapore, today announced that it has entered into a non-binding term sheet with Golden Concord Group Limited in relation to a proposed acquisition of a minority interest in its subsidiary Multi Genius Limited ("MGL").

Separately, Ryde has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") with GCL Digital Technology (Holdings) Limited ("GCL Digital"), a subsidiary of MGL, to explore potential technology collaboration.

The announcement follows Ryde's previously unveiled Ryde 2.0 transformation plan, which includes exploring new opportunities to strengthen the Company's technology capabilities and support long-term growth.

MGL, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the development of an energy-backed digital infrastructure platform with a focus on artificial intelligence ("AI") and high-performance computing ("HPC") technologies.

Under the indicative non-binding term sheet, Ryde is evaluating the potential acquisition of a minority equity interest in MGL, with an indicative aggregate transaction value of up to US$18 million. The final transaction structure, form and amount of consideration, valuation and other terms remain subject to due diligence, independent valuation, negotiation and definitive documentation.

The proposed investment forms part of Ryde's broader Ryde 2.0 strategy of selectively exploring partnerships and investments that could strengthen the Company's long-term technology capabilities. Ryde believes that advances in AI, computing infrastructure and cybersecurity may create opportunities to enhance its technology platform and support potential new areas of growth.

Separately, under the MOU with GCL Digital, the parties intend to explore potential collaboration across three areas: cybersecurity services, GPU computing infrastructure, and data centre operations and maintenance. The parties may also explore other mutually beneficial opportunities relating to AI, high-performance computing and digital infrastructure.

The MOU does not obligate either party to purchase, supply or procure any minimum quantity of hardware, infrastructure capacity or services, and any future commercial engagement would be subject to separate agreements.

The proposed investment in MGL and any potential procurement or technology collaboration under the MOU are being evaluated independently, and neither arrangement is conditional upon the other.

"Innovation has always been central to Ryde's long-term strategy," said a spokesperson for Ryde. "As we advance Ryde 2.0, we are exploring opportunities to strengthen our technology capabilities and participate selectively in emerging areas such as AI and digital infrastructure. GE Aerospace does not endorse Potemkin’s unsolicited mini-tender offer and recommends that GE Aerospace shareholders do not tender their shares in the offer because the offer is at a price significantly below the current market price for GE Aerospace’s shares.

Shareholders should obtain current market quotations for their shares, consult with their broker or financial advisor, and exercise caution with respect to Potemkin’s mini-tender offer. GE Aerospace recommends that shareholders who have not responded to Potemkin’s offer take no action. Shareholders who have already tendered their shares may withdraw them according to Potemkin’s offering documents.

Mini-tender offers seek to acquire less than five percent of a company's outstanding shares. Consequently, they can avoid many disclosure and procedural requirements of U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules that apply to offers for more than five percent of a company's outstanding shares.

The SEC has cautioned investors about mini-tender offers, stating that mini-tender offers “have been increasingly used to catch investors off guard,” and that investors “may end up selling their securities at below-market prices.” The SEC's guidance to investors on mini-tender offers is available at https://www.sec.gov/reportspubs/investor-publications/investorpubsminitendhtm.html.

GE Aerospace encourages brokers and dealers, as well as other market participants, to review the SEC's letter regarding broker-dealer mini-tender offer dissemination and disclosure available at https://www.sec.gov/divisions/marketreg/minitenders/sia072401.htm.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Review

Revenue from Cloud Mining Solutions for the third quarter of 2026 was $13.8 million, an 88.8% decrease from $122.9 million in the same period of 2025. This decline was primarily attributable to lower average selling prices, driven by lower year-over-year average BTC prices, and weaker market sentiment.

Revenue from Bitcoin self-mining operations in the third quarter of 2026 was $18.4 million, compared with $20.1 million in the same period of 2025. The year-over-year change primarily reflected the combined effect of: (1) a 38.0% decline in the average BTC price to $71,000 in the third quarter of 2026 from $114,500 in the third quarter of 2025; and (2) a 50.9% increase in average hashrate allocated to self-mining operations.

Revenue from mining equipment sales was $2.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $35.8 million in the same period of 2025, driven by lower customer demand amid Bitcoin price uncertainty and broader market sentiment.

Revenue from Hosting and Other was $3.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. The year-over-year increase was primarily driven by our Buy and Host one-stop solution, which continued to attract clients seeking asset ownership with simplified, hassle-free mining operations.

Cost of Revenue

Cost of revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $39.7 million, a decrease of 77.1% from $173.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly attributable to a reduction in scale.

The increase was primarily attributable to share-based compensation expenses of US$0.8 million, compared to less than US$0.1 million during the same period of 2025, partially offset by the absence of sales commission expenses, which amounted to US$0.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.

General and administrative expenses, and research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $2.1 million and $0.6 million, respectively. Excluding the increase in share-based compensation expenses of $0.3 million, these expenses were approximately in line with those in the same period of 2025.

Credit loss provision for other current assets was $2.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with nil in the same period of 2025. Of the $2.6 million provision, $2.05 million, representing 50% of the prepaid investment made in connection with the pending acquisition of a Bitcoin mining facility in Ethiopia, reflects the uncertainty around the transaction, as disclosed in the Company’s September 2026 operating update. The Company continues to actively pursue all available measures to protect its legal rights and financial interests, as well as those of its shareholders.

The Company recognized a $36.5 million fair value gain on digital assets and digital asset-related receivables or payables in the third quarter of 2026, reflecting the recovery in Bitcoin prices during the period. By comparison, the Company recognized a $10.0 million fair value gain in the third quarter of 2025.

Edmonton, Alberta – November 20, 2026 – TheNewswire - Bitcoin Well Inc. (“Bitcoin Well” or the “Company”) (TSXV: BTCW; OTCQB: BCNWF), the non-custodial bitcoin business on a mission to enable independence, today announced financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Key highlights

  • Revenue of $14.6 million for the 3-months ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 2025: $34.0 million, -57%) and $67.9 million for the 9-months ended September 30, 2026 (2025: $97.9 million, -31%). 

  • Over 82,000 unique users in the Bitcoin Portal as of September 30 2026 (+6% from June 30, 2026 and +44% from September 30, 2025). 

  • Gross profit of $0.8 million for the 3-months ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 2025: $1.3 million, -37%) and $2.9 million for the 9-months ended September 30, 2026 (2025: $3.8 million, -24%).  

    • Gross margin increased to 5.7% in Q3 2026 from 3.9% in Q3 2025 due to changes in sales mix and improved margins within both the Online Bitcoin Portal and Bitcoin Well Infinite business lines. 

    • Year-to date gross margin was 4.2% in 2026, compared to 3.8% in 2025. 

  • Adjusted EBITDA of negative $0.5 million for the 3-months ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 2025: negative $0.3 million) and negative $1.6 million for the 9-months ended September 30, 2026 (2025: negative $0.7 million). 

  • Total comprehensive income reached $1.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, marking a turnaround from a loss of $2.2 million in Q3 2025. For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, total comprehensive loss was $4.1 million, compared to a loss of $3.9 million in the prior-year period. 

    • The shift to positive total comprehensive income during Q3 2026 was driven by a recovery in bitcoin prices and the resulting appreciation of our bitcoin treasury assets. 

    • As of November 18, 2026, our Bitcoin Treasury retained a net position of approximately 69 bitcoin.

While Bitcoin Well experienced a slower quarter due to the challenging market environment throughout 2026, with top-line revenue contracting to $14.6 million in Q3 2026 and $67.9 million year-to-date, the Company maintained a clear focus on operational efficiency and margin optimization. Notably, gross margins expanded to 5.7% in Q3 2026, up from 3.9% in the prior year’s comparative period, reflecting an improved revenue mix and enhanced unit margins across its core business lines.

 

Total comprehensive income was positive $1.2 million in Q3 2026, a significant turnaround driven by the appreciation of the Company’s bitcoin treasury assets, which continues to be approximately 69 bitcoin. With registered users on the Online Bitcoin Portal now exceeding 82,000 and the deployment of key operational upgrades, Bitcoin Well continued to enhance both platform scalability and customer experience. These internal advancements are complemented by major strategic milestones, including the Company’s new partnership with Heritage IRA to introduce a Bitcoin IRA offering to US customers, which was launched in Q3 2026.

 

The Company remains confident in its outlook. By prioritizing operational excellence and deepening its strategic alliances, Bitcoin Well has solidified a strong foundation for the future. The Company anticipates that these foundational advancements will position Bitcoin Well to accelerate revenue growth and capture significant market opportunity as cryptocurrency market conditions normalize and improve.

   

Additional information

This news release should be read in concert with the full disclosure documents. The Bitcoin Well unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Management Discussion & Analysis for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 will be available on the Bitcoin Well website (www.bitcoinwell.com), via SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) or can be requested from the Company.

 

Closing of Debt Settlement

 

The Company also announces that, further to its news release dated October 16, 2026, it has completed its previously announced debt settlement pursuant to which it issued 5,733,187 common shares of the Company (each, a “Share”) at a deemed price of $0.045 per Share in full and final settlement of outstanding indebtedness in the amount of $257,993 (the “Indebtedness”). The Indebtedness related to interest owing on use of coin and debenture interest debt as of September 30, 2026, and the Shares were issued November 10, 2026 (the “Debt Settlement”).

 

The Debt Settlement remains subject to the final approval of the TSX Venture Exchange, and the securities issued in connection with the Debt Settlement are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, in accordance with applicable securities laws.

 

A director of the Company participated in the Debt Settlement through a wholly owned subsidiary. Such participation is considered to be a “related party transaction” within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”).

 

The Company intends to rely on the exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 contained in sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 in respect of the related party transaction in the Debt Settlement as neither the fair market value (as determined under MI 61-101) of the subject matter of, nor the fair market value of the consideration for, the transaction, insofar as it involves interested parties, is expected to exceed 25% of the Company’s market capitalization (as determined under MI 61-101).

Bitcoin Well is on a mission to enable independence. We do this by making bitcoin useful to everyday people to give them the convenience of modern banking and the benefits of bitcoin. We like to think of it as future-proofing money. Our existing Bitcoin ATM and Online Bitcoin Portal business units drive cash flow to help fund this mission.

Global travel rankings grow to 98 annual lists across nine regions and 22 languages, with the first standalone Oceania lists.

SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trip.Best, the global travel rankings from Trip.com Group, launched its 2027 Annual Rankings in Sydney, extending coverage to all seven continents for the first time. Unveiled at The Dome, Sydney Showground, as part of Trip.com Group's Global Partner Summit, this year's edition grows from 85 to 98 annual rankings and from five to nine regions, across 22 languages.

Oceania, Africa and Antarctica join as new regions, and the Americas are now split into North and South America. In total, the 2027 Annual Rankings feature more than 3,700 entries across 112 countries and regions, spanning hotels, attractions, nightlife, dining and destinations. Winners were recognised at the Global 100 Awards Ceremony.

Oceania Steps Into the Global Spotlight With Eight Standalone Rankings

For the first time, Trip.Best publishes eight standalone Oceania 50 lists, recognising more than 250 hotels, attractions, restaurants and experiences across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands. The lists cover scenic hotels, must-see and family attractions, nightlife, fine dining and must-visit restaurants, with ski-resort and hot-spring rankings reflecting the region's year-round appeal.

Top-ranked winners include:

  • Scenic Hotel: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora, followed by Park Hyatt Sydney and Rosewood Kauri Cliffs in New Zealand.
  • Best Things to Do: Sydney Opera House, followed by Bora Bora and the TSS Earnslaw Steamship in Queenstown.
  • Fine Dining: Essence in Queenstown, followed by Bennelong in Sydney and Jano Bistro in Wellington.
  • Must-Visit Restaurant: Fergburger in Queenstown, followed by Bar Totti's in Sydney and Depot in Auckland.

Global 100 Lists Honour Leading Hotels, Sights and Restaurants

At global level, the Global 100 lists are led by:

  • Luxury Hotel: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel in Paris, followed by Raffles Singapore and Le Bristol Paris.
  • Scenic Hotel: Il San Pietro di Positano in Italy, followed by Cheval Blanc Randheli in the Maldives and Le Sirenuse in Positano.
  • Best Things to Do: The Louvre in Paris.
  • Fine Dining: DiverXO in Madrid, followed by L'Arpège in Paris and Disfrutar in Barcelona.

New Wonders Lists Showcase What Makes a Destination Distinctive

Trip.Best also introduces Wonders - a new collection of rankings aimed at international travellers seeking inspiration for their next destination. Each list is built on what makes a destination distinctive and what gives it an edge over others across markets. The collection comprises 49 themed lists across 10 countries and four categories (hotels, attractions, food and destinations) and is available in 22 languages.

Australia features in two lists: Native Wildlife Conservation Encounters, led by Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary, and Outdoor Adventures, led by Cairns. Global Wonders lists include Diving Experiences, Ski Towns and Sunset Views.

  • Explore the full Trip.Best 2027 rankings here

About Trip.com Group

Trip.com Group is a leading global travel service provider comprising of Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner, and Qunar. Across its platforms, Trip.com Group helps travellers around the world make informed and cost-effective bookings for travel products and services and enables partners to connect their offerings with users through the aggregation of comprehensive travel-related content and resources, and an advanced transaction platform consisting of apps, websites and 24/7 customer service centres. Founded in 1999 and listed on NASDAQ in 2003 and HKEX in 2021, Trip.com Group has become one of the best-known travel groups in the world, with the mission "to pursue the perfect trip for a better world".
